references.text: Describes similar curses where enemies will eat what is sown, as part of the covenant's curses
A prophetic promise that enemies will no longer eat the grain, in contrast to the curse in Deuteronomy
Mentions grain, wine, and oil that God will send to the people, the same elements mentioned in the curse
Mentions the firstfruits of grain, wine, and oil given to the priests - the same products threatened in the curse
Uses the same terminology regarding offspring of livestock and lambs, as blessings God gives through obedience
The promise of grain, wine, and oil as a blessing for obedience - opposite of the curse
Historical fulfillment where the Midianites destroyed Israel's crops and livestock
A prophecy that enemies will devour the harvest, the small livestock and the cattle - a direct parallel to the curse
